summary.text: Rachel Talbot Ross is a Democratic state senator from Maine Senate District 28 who took office on December 3, 2024, and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2016 to 2024, including as the first Black speaker of the Maine House.

paragraphs.text: Rachel Talbot Ross worked as the City of Portland's director of equal opportunity and multicultural affairs for 20 years and as president of the Portland branch of the NAACP.
She founded three nonprofit organizations focused on racial justice in Maine and chaired the Maine Advisory Committee to the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights.
Talbot Ross first ran for public office in 2016, winning a seat in the Maine House in District 40; after redistricting she won election in District 118.
She became assistant majority leader in November 2020, and the House unanimously elected her Speaker in November 2022.

She sponsored legislation to create Maine's Permanent Commission on the Status of Racial, Indigenous and Tribal Populations, which she chaired, and bills to include racial impact analysis in the legislative process.
